# A page's var read before a nested local of its name: `seen = count` reads
# the page's `count`, and the `var count` the `if` declares after it is that
# block's own. Kotlin bound every local a body declares for the whole body
# (codegen.BodyLocals), and told a write of the state from the local by its
# symbol but a read by its name, so the read came out a bare `count` the test
# build's state class had no such name for, and android did not build.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main ui.node {
    var count = 1
    var seen = 0
    ui.button #bump(text="bump", @click {
        seen = count
        if seen > 0 {
            var count = 100
            seen = seen + count
        }
        count = count + 1
    })
}

func testAStateReadBeforeANestedLocalOfItsName(t Test, c main) {
    c.bump.click()
    t.assert(c.seen == 101)
    t.assert(c.count == 2)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
